summary:
Stage 5 (C6, paper-slide-deck proofread gate, commit 3e56794 at head db01216) targets-only review. The core gate logic in proofread.ts (proofreadGate) is well covered by unit tests for status, sha binding, [CHECK], allow flag, missing generated.json and an unreadable ledger. Two C6 clauses have no test at the level the criterion states, though. First, nothing tests that generate-slides.py main() actually calls record_generated. Second, nothing asserts what the merge scripts print: the slide names, the [CHECK] lines or the warning. Both blocking findings below are mutants that would survive. Separately, several documented workflows let an unproofread AI slide reach the PPTX/PDF without the gate firing: renumbering/renaming, the Gemini Web path, slides skipped as already generated, and a deleted generated.json.

Mutation targets (selected by: adversary, claude subagent), with the test that must fail:
1. C6 clause 1 (record filename+sha256) - generate-slides.py record_generated line ~224: replace hashlib.sha256(output_path.read_bytes()).hexdigest() with hashlib.sha256(b"").hexdigest(). Must fail: tests/test_generate_slides.py::test_record_generated_writes_sha_prompt_and_model.
2. C6 clause 1 (every slide; keeps others) - generate-slides.py line 215: replace `.get("slides", {})` with `{}` (drop prior records). Must fail: test_record_generated_keeps_other_slides_and_replaces_a_new_extension (01-slide-cover.png missing).
3. C6 clause 1 (regenerated under new ext replaces record) - generate-slides.py stem filter: change `Path(name).stem != stem` to `True`. Must fail: test_record_generated_keeps_other_slides_and_replaces_a_new_extension (02-slide-x.png lingers).
4. C6 clause 1 (wiring) - generate-slides.py line 330: delete the `record_generated(deck_dir, written, ...)` call in main(). EXPECTED SURVIVOR: no test drives main(); see finding 1. A test with a stub client/types (or factoring the loop body into a testable function) must be added and must then kill this.
5. C6 clause 2 (no proofread entry -> refuse) - proofread.ts line 61: change `!entry || !STATUSES.has(...)` to `!STATUSES.has(entry?.status ?? "ok")` (missing entry treated as ok). The sha branch then also fails on undefined. Simpler variant: change the line-59 guard to `if (slide.filename in generated) continue;`. Must fail: proofread.test.mjs 'an unproofread generated slide is fatal and named; the extracted slide is not' and both '<merge> refuses an unproofread deck and writes nothing'.
6. C6 clause 2 (sha mismatch -> refuse) - proofread.ts line 63: change `entry.sha256 !== sha256File(slide.path)` to `false`. Must fail: 'a slide changed after proofreading is unproofread again'.
7. C6 clause 2 (status must be ok|check) - proofread.ts line 61: drop `|| !STATUSES.has(entry.status ?? "")`. Must fail: 'an invalid status is not a disposition'.
8. C6 clause 2 (merge pptx wiring) - merge-to-pptx.ts line 259: pass `{ allowUnproofread: true }` to proofreadGate (or replace the `!== 0` test with `=== 2`). Must fail: 'merge-to-pptx refuses an unproofread deck and writes nothing'.
9. C6 clause 2 (merge pdf wiring) - merge-to-pdf.ts line 234: same mutation as 8. Must fail: 'merge-to-pdf refuses an unproofread deck and writes nothing'.
10. C6 clause 2 (naming EACH slide) - proofread.ts loop line 58: add `break` after the first `unproofread.push`. EXPECTED SURVIVOR: every fixture has exactly one generated slide. Add a fixture with two unproofread generated slides and assert both names appear.
11. C6 clause 2 (merge names the slide) - proofread.ts line 80: delete `for (const f of result.fatal) console.error(...)`. EXPECTED SURVIVOR: merge tests check only the exit code; see finding 2.
12. C6 clause 3 ([CHECK] allowed) - proofread.ts line 62/66 ordering: move the `entry.status === "check"` case into the unproofread branch (treat check as fatal). Must fail: 'a check disposition is allowed but listed with its note'.
13. C6 clause 3 ([CHECK] listed by the merge) - proofread.ts line 78: delete the `[CHECK]` print loop. EXPECTED SURVIVOR: no merge-level test uses a check disposition or captures stderr; see finding 2.
14. C6 clause 4 (--allow-unproofread downgrades) - proofread.ts line 71: replace `(allowUnproofread ? warnings : fatal)` with `fatal`. Must fail: '--allow-unproofread turns the refusal into a warning' and both '<merge> merges with --allow-unproofread, and after proofreading'.
15. C6 clause 4 (flag parsing) - merge-to-pdf.ts parseArgs: change the literal '--allow-unproofread' to '--allow-unproofed'. Must fail: 'merge-to-pdf merges with --allow-unproofread, and after proofreading'. Apply the same to merge-to-pptx.ts.
16. C6 clause 4 (printed warning) - proofread.ts line 79: delete the warning print loop. EXPECTED SURVIVOR: see finding 2.
17. C6 clause 5 (no generated.json unaffected) - proofread.ts line 46: replace the early return with `fatal.push("no generated.json")` (fail closed). Must fail: 'a deck without generated.json (extract-only) is not gated'. Note that simply deleting line 46 is an equivalent mutant (readSlides returns {} for a missing file), so do not choose that one.
18. C6 unreadable ledger - proofread.ts: drop the try/catch and let readSlides errors be swallowed as `{}` (wrap readSlides in try { } catch { return {} }). Must fail: 'an unreadable ledger is fatal, not nothing to proofread'.
19. markProofread binds the sha - proofread.ts markProofread: store `sha256: ""`. Must fail: 'an ok disposition on the same bytes passes' and both '<merge> merges ... after proofreading'.

Detector weaknesses / bypasses reported as findings: (1) the generate-slides main() wiring is untested; (2) the merge-level stderr naming, [CHECK] listing and warning are untested; (3) the gate is keyed by exact filename, so the skill's own renumber/reslug workflow (and case-only renames) makes a recorded generated slide invisible to the gate; (4) the Gemini Web path never writes generated.json; slides skipped by existing_output are never recorded; a deleted generated.json disables the gate. All of these fail open, while SKILL.md claims every generated slide is proofread before merge; (5) a generated slide placed in slides/ is gated, but markProofread can only mark root files, so the only way out is --allow-unproofread.

findings.title: generate-slides.py main() never exercised: removing the record_generated call survives
findings.what_goes_wrong: C6 clause 1 says generate-slides.py records every slide it writes. The only tests call record_generated() directly (tests/test_generate_slides.py, the two test_record_generated_* tests). If the call at line 330 is deleted, or moved under a wrong condition (e.g. only when success_count == 0), generated.json is never written. Every C6 test still passes, and the merge gate then sees no generated.json and treats the deck as extract-only, so it does not gate at all.
findings.why_vulnerable: main() needs a google-genai client, so the author tested the helper in isolation. The clause that matters, that the script writes the ledger for each generated slide, is the wiring, and nothing covers it. Because a missing ledger fails open by design, this mutation silently disables the whole Step 6.5 gate.
findings.how_to_confirm: Snapshot inspection: grep the two tests for main( or generate_slide; there are no hits. Mutation target 4: delete line 330 and run `python3 -m pytest paper-slide-deck/tests/`. All tests pass.
findings.recommendation: Factor the per-slide loop body into a function (e.g. generate_and_record(client, types, model, slide, deck_dir)), or monkeypatch generate_slide in a test of main(), so that a stubbed generation writes a file. Then assert that generated.json lists it with the file's sha256. That kills mutant 4.

findings.title: Merge-level naming, [CHECK] listing and override warning are unasserted (reportProofread print loops can be deleted)
findings.what_goes_wrong: C6 requires the merge scripts to exit non-zero naming each offending slide, to list [CHECK] entries, and to print a warning under --allow-unproofread. The merge tests in proofread.test.mjs (the for-loop over merge-to-pptx/merge-to-pdf) assert only the return code and whether an output file exists. They never capture stderr, and no merge test uses a check disposition. Deleting any of the three console.error loops at lines 78-80 survives (targets 11, 13, 16). So does adding `break` in the proofreadGate loop so that only the first slide is named (target 10), because every fixture has a single generated slide.
findings.why_vulnerable: Names and [CHECK] text are produced in proofreadGate (unit-tested), but only reportProofread prints them. reportProofread has no direct test, and the merge tests do not observe its output. The user-visible half of the criterion therefore has no detector.
findings.how_to_confirm: Read tests/proofread.test.mjs. No test calls reportProofread or stubs console.error, and every deck() fixture defaults to generated=['02-slide-method.png']. Apply target 13 (delete line 78) and run `node --test paper-slide-deck/tests/*.mjs`: it stays green.
findings.recommendation: Stub console.error in the merge tests and assert that: the refusal names 02-slide-method.png; a `check` disposition yields exit 0 plus a '[CHECK] 02-slide-method.png — note' line; --allow-unproofread prints 'Warning:' naming the slide. Add a two-unproofread-slide fixture and assert that both names appear.

findings.title: Gate keyed by exact filename: the skill's documented renumber/reslug workflow lets unproofread generated slides merge silently
findings.what_goes_wrong: proofreadGate skips any slide whose filename is not a key in generated.json (line 59), and silently ignores recorded keys with no file on disk. references/modification-guide.md (Add/Delete slide, lines 22 and 34) tells the agent to renumber files, e.g. 04-slide-conclusion.png -> 05-slide-conclusion.png, and to change the slug when content changes. After that, a generated slide that was never proofread has a name not in generated.json and is merged with no error, warning or [CHECK]. A case-only rename (02-slide-x.png -> 02-slide-x.PNG) also escapes, because SLIDE_PATTERN in the merge scripts is case-insensitive but the ledger lookup is case-sensitive. The same holds on case-insensitive filesystems.
findings.why_vulnerable: The record binds identity to the filename rather than to the bytes, and a recorded entry with no matching file is never reported. The strict C6 wording (each recorded slide) is satisfied only because the recorded name no longer exists, while the gate's purpose is defeated. This is inferred from the code and the docs; not reproduced.
findings.how_to_confirm: Fixture: generated.json lists 02-slide-method.png, with no proofread.json. Rename the file to 03-slide-method.png and call proofreadGate with the renamed slide: fatal == []. The same with 02-slide-method.PNG.
findings.recommendation: Also match by content: treat any merged slide whose sha256 equals a recorded generated sha256 as generated. Fail (or at least warn) when a generated.json key has no file on disk ('recorded slide missing — renamed?'). Compare names case-insensitively. Update modification-guide.md to rename the generated.json/proofread.json keys with the files, or to re-run proofread.

findings.title: Fail-open paths: Gemini Web generation, skipped-as-existing slides and a deleted generated.json bypass the gate, contradicting SKILL.md
findings.what_goes_wrong: SKILL.md line 8 claims 'every generated slide is proofread before it can be merged'. But: (a) Option 2 (references/gemini-web.md, baoyu-danger-gemini-web main.ts --image NN-slide-x.png) never writes generated.json, so those AI slides are ungated; (b) find_slides_to_generate skips any slide with an existing >10KB output (generate-slides.py line 238) without recording it. Slides generated before this change, by Gemini Web, or by a run that crashed between write and record_generated therefore stay unrecorded forever; (c) deleting generated.json (or never having one) makes proofreadGate return early (proofread.ts line 46), so every slide merges with no warning at all.
findings.why_vulnerable: The gate is opt-in on a file that only one of the two documented generators writes. Absence of the ledger is indistinguishable from an extract-only deck, which C6 requires to be unaffected, so there is no signal.
findings.how_to_confirm: Read gemini-web.md 'Per-slide invocation': there is no proofread/generated step. Read generate-slides.py lines 229-240: skipped slides are not passed to record_generated. Read proofread.ts line 46.
findings.recommendation: Document in gemini-web.md that each Option 2 slide must be recorded, and add a `proofread.ts --record <deck> <slide>` helper. In generate-slides.py, record skipped existing outputs that are absent from generated.json, or warn about them. At merge time, if prompts/ exists and a slide has a matching prompt but no generated.json entry, warn that it looks AI-generated but is unrecorded. Soften the SKILL.md line 8 claim to match.

findings.title: Generated slide located in slides/ is gated but cannot be marked: markProofread resolves only the deck root
findings.what_goes_wrong: The merge scripts scan both the deck root and slides/ (merge-to-pptx.ts lines 90-92), and the gate hashes slide.path, which may be in slides/. markProofread uses join(dir, filename), so `--mark <deck> 02-slide-x.png ok` for a recorded slide that lives only in slides/ throws 'slide not found'. The only way to merge is then --allow-unproofread, which teaches the override. Related: when the root and slides/ both hold the same filename, the root copy wins and is hashed. That is consistent with what is merged, so it is not a bypass.
findings.why_vulnerable: The path resolution in markProofread is inconsistent with findSlideImages.
findings.how_to_confirm: Fixture: generated.json lists 02-slide-x.png, and the file exists only in slides/. proofreadGate reports it fatal; markProofread(dir, '02-slide-x.png', 'ok') throws.
findings.recommendation: Resolve the slide in markProofread with the same root-then-slides/ order as findSlideImages, and add a test for it.

limits: snapshot-only; no command reproduction; no OS sandbox; reviewer: claude subagent (same model family as author). Inspected base 98b1ffe...head db01216 diff for paper-slide-deck plus surrounding code (findSlideImages, generate_slide, find_slides_to_generate, gemini-web.md, modification-guide.md). No mutant was executed: survivor/killed predictions are from reading the tests. No evidence files were cited, so verify-evidence.sh was not run. The external baoyu-danger-gemini-web skill is not in the repo; its behavior is inferred from gemini-web.md. Node's ability to import .ts in the gate (type stripping) was not checked.
